items.title: Albert Artigues Sr. Interview, 1961-12-15
items.q: I used to always, wherever Sharky played I'd be, when I was a youngster. And, uh, sitting with Sharky, Sharky let me, you know, take down and let me do most of the driving.

ctx.x: uncle or grandfather, anybody play music? Nobody in the family played music. I'm the only one in the family. How in the world did you ever get interested?

I don't know. I just saw a horn and liked it, picked it up. I was going to Holy Cross College at the time and got planted by ear. Never did. No, I started to take a few lessons at school. And I wanted to play Dixieland music and the brother wanted me to play march music. So it didn't jive. I quit the class real soon and got to playing by ear, you know. And I formed my own band. After a while I went with Joe Kless's band. From there, Sharky left to go with the Wolverines in New York and Norman Brownlee took me to…
